stem: An operon is a section of DNA found in prokaryotes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why the enzymes coded for by the *lac* operon are described as inducible enzymes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
An investigation into the induction and action of the *lac* operon was carried out using the bacterium, *Escherichia coli*, grown in a growth medium containing glucose.

When the bacteria had used all the glucose, an excess of lactose was added to the growth medium. The activity of $\beta$-galactosidase was measured from this time ($0\text{ min}$), as shown in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:figure_3_1.png}}

Fig. 3.1

With reference to the *lac* operon, explain the shape of the curve in Fig. 3.1.
